description:
FILED s473t6d member 4 (Opus, 2026-09-20, finished s493), found by the t/op/magic.t
row that #1954 re-aligned.

perl's `$^S` is THREE-valued: undef while COMPILING (inside any BEGIN block), 0 at
run time, 1 inside an eval.  cl/pcl-runtime.lisp has only the last two
(`(defvar |$^S| 0 "Perl $^S - eval state: 0 runtime, 1 inside eval")`, and the two
binding sites bind it to 1), so the compile-phase state is missing.

REPRO (scratchpad p-caretS.pl):

    print "runtime: ", (defined($^S) ? "defined=$^S" : "undef"), "\n";
    eval { print "in eval: ", (defined($^S) ? "defined=$^S" : "undef"), "\n" };
    eval ' BEGIN { print "BEGIN in string eval: ", (defined($^S) ? "defined=$^S" : "undef"), "\n" } ';
    BEGIN { print "BEGIN at file level: ", (defined($^S) ? "defined=$^S" : "undef"), "\n" }

    perl                        PCL
    BEGIN at file level: undef  BEGIN at file level: defined=0
    runtime: defined=0          runtime: defined=0
    in eval: defined=1          in eval: defined=1
    BEGIN in string eval: undef BEGIN in string eval: defined=1

ROWS BEHIND IT: t/op/magic.t perl row 124, `eval " BEGIN { ok ! defined \$^S } "`
(magic.t:615) -- one blessed companion fail row, now carrying this number.

SHAPE OF THE FIX: bind `|$^S|` to the undef box around every compile-phase body
(the eval-when :compile-toplevel BEGIN lowering, and the string-eval compile
phase), the same way the eval sites bind it to 1.  Cheap; the only question is
whether every BEGIN path goes through one place.
subject: `$^S` is not UNDEF during compilation: PCL answers 0 in a file-level BEGIN and 1 in a string eval's BEGIN, where perl answers undef in both
